name: dup
synopsis: int dup3(int oldfd, int newfd, int flags);
description: The dup() system call creates a copy of a file descriptor. dup2() duplicates a file descriptor to a specified new descriptor, closing the new one if it was open. dup3() is similar to dup2() but allows additional flags and disallows duplicating to the same descriptor.

parameters.name: oldfd
parameters.description: The file descriptor to be duplicated

parameters.name: newfd
parameters.description: The new file descriptor number to use (for dup2 and dup3)

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for dup3, such as O_CLOEXEC to set close-on-exec

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: oldfd isn’t an open file descriptor
newfd is out of the allowed range for file descriptors
This may be returned by dup2() or dup3() during a race condition with open(2) and dup()
The dup2() or dup3() call was interrupted by a signal
The per-process limit on the number of open file descriptors has been reached

bugs: dup2() does not report errors from closing newfd, and implementing equivalent functionality with close and dup may lead to race conditions.
versions: dup() and dup2(): POSIX.1-2001; dup3(): Linux 2.6.27
